questions.prompt: `readdir` returns the names `.` and `..` among the entries. To skip them you compare `d_name` with...
questions.explain: `d_name` is a string, so compare it with `strcmp(name, ".") == 0`. `.` is the directory itself and `..` its parent; hidden files such as `.profile` are real entries and must not be skipped by mistake.

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (Counting entries.)
questions.explain: The directory holds `a`, `b` and the hidden `.c`. `readdir` also returns `.` and `..`, which the loop skips, so the count is 3.

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (chdir changes the program's own directory.)
questions.explain: After `chdir("sub")`, `getcwd` returns the absolute path ending in `/sub`; `strrchr(cwd, '/') + 1` skips to the last component.

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (The reason of a failure.)
questions.explain: `opendir` returns NULL when it fails and sets `errno` (here `ENOENT`); `strerror` turns it into text.

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (rmdir only removes empty directories.)
questions.explain: `rmdir` refuses a directory that still has entries (`ENOTEMPTY`): remove the files first.

questions.prompt: In which order does `readdir` return the entries of a directory?
questions.explain: The order depends on the file system. Collect the names (copy them with `strdup`) and sort with `qsort`.
options: No particular order: sort them yourself if you need one

questions.prompt: A program calls `chdir("/tmp")`. What happens to the shell that started it?
questions.explain: Each process has its own current directory. This is why `cd` has to be a built-in command of the shell, not a program.
options: Nothing: the program changes only its own working directory
Only the next command is affected
option_notes: Processes cannot change their parent's directory.
No effect on the shell at all.

questions.explain: `DIR *d = opendir(path)` opens the directory; each `readdir(d)` returns a pointer to the next entry (its name is `d_name`) or NULL when there are no more.
options: A `DIR *` (NULL on error) and a `struct dirent *` (NULL at the end)
option_notes: They use special types, not descriptors.
The name is a member of the returned structure.

questions.prompt: Which statements about the entries `.` and `..` are true?
questions.explain: Both appear in every directory listing returned by `readdir`; programs usually skip them with `strcmp`.
options: `readdir` returns them like any other entry

questions.prompt: To get the next entry of an open directory you call {{0}}.
questions.explain: `readdir(dir)` returns the next entry, or NULL at the end.

questions.prompt: Match each directory function with what it does.
pairs: gives the absolute path of the current directory
changes the current directory of the program

questions.prompt: Put the steps of listing a directory in order.
questions.explain: Open, check, loop until the end, then close.
items: Check that the result is not NULL
Call readdir in a loop until it returns NULL

questions.prompt: What does this program print? (rewinddir starts again.)
questions.explain: After the first loop the directory is exhausted; `rewinddir` moves back to the first entry, so the second loop sees the same entries.
